For example, a countermovement jump involves a quick lowering of the body to produce eccentric tension in the relevant musculature which is then followed by a transition from down to up, the amortization phase, and then the athlete develops concentric or shortening tension in the relevant muscles as he/she performs the 'up' phase of the jump.
